scope: Cloud proxy samples only. Not PS4 bandwidth, not full-package integrity. Up to12MiB total payload across3games, plus3240headerbytes.
method: One sequential 2 MiB byte range versus two concurrent adjacent 1 MiB ranges from the same approved final HTTPS URL; exact 206, Content-Range, Content-Length and equal strong ETag validated. Samples were compared byte-for-byte.
limitations: Small public samples through the development proxy, not a sustained PS4 test.
Sample hashes identify only the sampled bytes; no complete PKG was downloaded or hashed.
This does not predict bandwidth on the user’s Claro Wi-Fi or guarantee a speed increase.

buffer_revision.allocation_policy: Allocate both preferred transfer buffers or free them and retry both fallback buffers. Post-download hashing uses one buffer with the same bounded fallback.
buffer_revision.normal_transfer: Two 1 MiB (or both 256 KiB fallback) buffers alternate reception and disk/hash work. A caller-owned 16 KiB stdio tail buffer remains alive through fflush/fclose. Short fragments are coalesced while every native read retains PKG identity validation, progress and cancellation.
buffer_revision.parallel_eligibility: Already approved final Archive, GitHub and MediaFire CDN HTTPS URLs only. Requires pinned Content ID/kind/size, strong identical ETags, exact 206 and range lengths, and assembled PKG verification. Missing validators or rejected range setup retain/restart the normal stream once.
buffer_revision.eof_error_regression: Verified Content-Length ends the body without waiting for another EOF read; unknown-length bodies still require actual EOF.

host_fixture_results.normal_1_mib_fixture: One data read at preferred capacity versus four at fallback/previous capacity, when the mock server fills the requested buffer.
host_fixture_results.parallel_32_mib_fragmented_fixture: 32 disk writes at preferred capacity versus 128 at previous/fallback capacity; the same 2048 native short reads for 16 KiB fragments.
host_fixture_results.validation: Exact byte comparison, SHA-256, failed preferred/fallback allocations, safe buffer lifetime, cancellation, range redirects, wrong identities/kinds, truncation, and prior completed-file preservation.

limitations: Fixture call counts are algorithm checks, not measured network speed or PS4 hardware tests.
The 1 MiB cap is deliberate. No real-console maximum buffer or throughput guarantee has been established.
This does not change HTTP/SSL native pool sizes, disable TLS validation, bypass proxy rules, or add download hosts.

single_stream_pipeline_revision.behavior: One validated HTTP response, a bounded two-slot queue and a joined native SCE pthread disk/hash worker. Network reception can overlap the previous block write. No extra server connection or unsupported host is introduced.
single_stream_pipeline_revision.thread_setup_fallback: Failure to create the additional worker before response data is consumed continues the same response synchronously using identical validation and framing.
single_stream_pipeline_revision.actual_mode_reporting: DownloadSnapshot distinguishes connecting, synchronous single response, pipelined single response and two validated byte-range responses; connection counts are 0, 1, 1 and 2 respectively.
host_validation: Held first disk write while requiring reception of the next 1 MiB block, then exact output comparison with and without SHA-256.
Disk failure aborts a blocked HTTP receiver without replacing the original disk error with the induced network abort.
Partial writes fail and preserve the previous completed package.
Cancellation and a transient failed first join retain file and buffer ownership until the worker finishes and is joined.
Existing known Content-Length EOF timeout 0x80431068, unknown-length EOF, package identity/kind/size and two-range fallback regressions retained.
single_stream_pipeline_revision.limits: Deterministic concurrency and integrity tests, not a measured PS4 speed increase. Hosting limits, Wi-Fi conditions, console disk speed and native HTTP behavior can still limit throughput.
